questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Bulgaria?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Bulgaria article.

questions.proof: The capital and the biggest city is Sofia.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Bulgaria?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Bulgaria on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Bulgaria article.

questions.proof: Bulgaria borders Romania, Serbia, North Macedonia, Greece, Turkey, and the Black Sea.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Bulgaria?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Bulgaria article.

questions.proof: Bulgaria has its own language, called Bulgarian.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “In 1997, Bulgaria and _____ signed a treaty to define the maritime boundary between them.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “signed”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Maritime waters” part of the Bulgaria article.

questions.proof: In 1997, Bulgaria and Turkey signed a treaty to define the maritime boundary between them.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Bulgaria's territorial waters border those of _____, Turkey and Ukraine.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “Turkey”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Maritime waters” part of the Bulgaria article.

questions.proof: Bulgaria's territorial waters border those of Romania, Turkey and Ukraine.
